finding_key: .github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml::`allowed_bots` disables claude-code-action's actor (non-bot) guard on the two secret-bearing, contents:write, bash-enabled agent jobs, making a fully human-free execution path for prompts built from untrusted branch output
evidence: The data path is real — verify-self.mjs writes `failureSummary: extractFailureSummary(output)` from raw lane output, summarize-ci.mjs prints it verbatim, and agent-iterate-ci.yml interpolates it into the prompt of a Bash-enabled, contents:write, secret-bearing step. But the claim misreads the change on two points: the value is `"yorkie-agent[bot],yorkie-agent"`, not `*`, so the actor guard is narrowed to the repo's own App rather than disabled; and that guard was never a human-in-the-loop control — a bot-initiated run just errors out (which is exactly why this same PR adds `needs.fix.result == 'failure'` to the `stalled` pager). The real human gates (AGENT_PIPELINE_ENABLED, fork-origin rejection, protected `agent` environment, branch-protection approval) are unchanged, and the injection-into-autonomous-agent surface pre-exists this line (the same job already runs `pnpm install` on branch code with the App token, and agent-implement.yml already feeds an untrusted issue body to an unrestricted-Bash agent) and is documented as an accepted residual risk in docs/design/harness-engineering.md. Without `allowed_bots` the loop cannot run at all, so this is the intended enablement, not a newly introduced defect; the only actionable item is verifying repo environment settings. I could not read claude-code-action's source (not supplied), so my reading of the guard's exact semantics comes from the input name and the in-repo comments.
